claim: test_history_templates.md E3: "Given `br list --json` returns invalid JSON (e.g., truncated output). When `ShowHistory` is called. Then: Function returns an error wrapping the JSON parse failure. Error message includes context about what was being parsed (\"task list output\")." E5 similarly asserts: "Task listing is done once (single `br list --json` call)."
authoritative_source: arch_history_viewer.md's Setup and Interface sections: "There is no mock tracker CLI: `ShowHistory` takes parsed task records and starts no process (`proposal/history.go:71`)" and "The viewer consumes four things and reaches for nothing else: the task records its caller has already parsed..." arch_proposal_commands.md assigns the stdin read and JSON decode, plus the `spex log: parse task JSON: <detail>` error message, to ProposalCommands, not HistoryViewer.
evidence: `ShowHistory([]TaskRecord)` never invokes `br list --json` and never parses JSON — both are ProposalCommands' responsibility per arch_proposal_commands.md's stdin contract. E3's precondition (malformed JSON from `br list --json`) and its expected error wrapping "task list output" describe a code path that does not exist in HistoryViewer; nothing in this component can produce that error. E5's "single `br list --json` call" clause is the same stale precondition — HistoryViewer never calls it at all, once or otherwise. Test section `b313b3531f32` (HistoryViewer Scenarios/Edge Cases) is this bead's own test leaf; the JSON-parse error path these cases describe belongs to ProposalCommands (bead spexmachina-swvx.18), which has no test coverage yet and is out of this bead's scope, so neither edge case can be discharged here.
proposed_fix: Retire E3 from test_history_templates.md's HistoryViewer Edge Cases (or move it, reworded around `spex log: parse task JSON: <detail>`, into a ProposalCommands test leaf once one exists). Reword E5 to drop the "single `br list --json` call" clause, keeping only the in-memory-filtering/large-input assertion that still applies to `ShowHistory`.
